    include-in-header:
      # The author redefinition the extension documents, and the only way a

The fixture for a principal mention in a heading and in a figure or table
caption (M114). LaTeX copies a heading into the contents list and the running
head, and a caption into the list of figures or tables. This page prints all
three lists, so it carries a copy of every heading the contents list shows
and of every caption below. Each term below is marked here too: [aster]{.index},
[basil]{.index}, [clover]{.index}, [dahlia]{.index}, [elm]{.index},
[fern]{.index}, [ginkgo]{.index} and [holly]{.index}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# The [aster]{.index mention="principal"} section

A principal mention in a level-one heading.

## The [basil]{.index mention="principal"} subsection

A principal mention in a level-two heading.

{{< pagebreak >}}

#### The [clover]{.index mention="principal"} paragraph

A principal mention in a level-four heading, `\paragraph`, which Quarto's
template sets on a line of its own.

{{< pagebreak >}}

This page's running head is a copy of the aster section's heading, and
aster is marked here: [aster]{.index}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# The [dahlia]{.index mention="principal" range="open"} section

A principal range opens in this heading.

{{< pagebreak >}}

This page's running head is a copy of the dahlia section's heading.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# The [dahlia]{.index range="close"} closing section

The range closes in this heading.

{{< pagebreak >}}

This page's running head is a copy of the closing section's heading.

{{< pagebreak >}}

So is this page's, and dahlia is marked here: [dahlia]{.index}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# The [holly]{.index} section

An ordinary mark in a heading.
